## Decision Memo: Truthful Finite Value Menus for `/agent` Options

### Current state

The shipped autocomplete has live value menus for three completion domains: `"thinking"` (7-level static enum), `"model"` (live `ctx.modelRegistry.getAll()`), and `"provider"` (derived from models). Four path-valued options (`--skill`, `--extension`, `--prompt-template`, `--theme`) use `completionDomain: "path"` for filesystem completion. ### The one real UX complication: comma-separated multi-value

`--tools read,bash,wr|` (cursor after `wr`) should complete the fragment `wr` against the tool catalog, excluding already-listed `read` and `bash`. 1. Recognize the comma-separated structure within the value token.
2. Extract the active fragment as the text after the last `,` (or the full value if no comma).
3. Exclude already-mentioned tool names from candidates.
4. Apply the completion to only the active fragment, preserving the `read,bash,` prefix.
5. After accepting a tool, insert a `,` (not a space) so the user can keep adding — unless this is the last one, where a space is correct. One pragmatic approach: always append `,` and let the user delete it or type a space when done.

This is a bounded extension to `ValueCursorExpectation` (add fragment-within-comma tracking) and `applyCompletionEdit` (replace only the post-comma portion). It does not require rethinking the grammar — the parser's value token boundary stays the same; the comma logic lives inside the `"tool"` domain's candidate/edit adapter.

1. A new `ValueCompletionDomain` variant `"tool"` in `command-line.ts`.
2. Setting `completionDomain: "tool"` on the two option definitions.
3. Passing a `getTools` callback (alongside the existing `getModels`) into `createAgentAutocompleteProvider`.
4. Comma-aware candidate generation and edit application in `autocomplete.ts`.

## Revised Decision Memo: Truthful Finite Value Menus — Round 2

### What `getCommands()` actually exposes

`pi.getCommands()` (on `ExtensionAPI`, the `pi` object — not on `ctx`) returns `SlashCommandInfo[]` built from three sources at runtime (`agent-session.js:_bindExtensionCore`):

| `source` | `name` shape | `sourceInfo.path` | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"skill"` | `"skill:${skill.name}"` | Absolute path to skill file (e.g. `SKILL.md`) | Every currently loaded skill |
| `"prompt"` | `template.name` | Absolute path to prompt template file | Every loaded prompt template |
| `"extension"` | `command.invocationName` | Extension's own source path | Registered commands, not extension paths |

The `sourceInfo.path` on skills and prompt templates is the same `filePath` the resource loader used to load them — exactly the format `--skill` and `--prompt-template` expect on the CLI. So the name→path mapping is already done for us.

`pi.getAllTools()` returns `ToolInfo[]` with `.name` for tool name completion. Both `pi.getAllTools()` and `pi.getCommands()` are lazily resolved through the runtime proxy (start as `notInitialized`, populated by `bindCore()` during session init, called during user typing after session is live). Same lifecycle safety as the existing `ctx.modelRegistry.getAll()` closure.

### Reconciliation: what each option should complete against

| Option | Current domain | Best available catalog | API | Insert value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--tools`, `--exclude-tools` | *none* (falls through silently) | `pi.getAllTools()` | `ToolInfo[].name` | Tool name |
| `--skill` | `"path"` | `pi.getCommands()`, `source === "skill"` | `sourceInfo.path` | Absolute file path |
| `--prompt-template` | `"path"` | `pi.getCommands()`, `source === "prompt"` | `sourceInfo.path` | Absolute file path |
| `--theme` | `"path"` | `getAvailableThemesWithPaths()` (importable) | `ThemeInfo.path` | Absolute file path |
| `--extension` | `"path"` | None clean — extensions in `getCommands()` are already-loaded commands, not loadable paths | — | Keep filesystem |

### What prompt templates and themes look like

Prompt templates in `getCommands()` carry the same `sourceInfo.path` that the resource loader consumed, so the inserted value is directly usable as a `--prompt-template` argument. Same for skills.

Themes have a separate importable function (`getAvailableThemesWithPaths()` from `theme.js:340`), not on any context object. It discovers built-in themes (`dark`, `light`) plus custom themes from `~/.pi/agent/themes/`. Each entry carries `{ name, path }`. Right now the user has six: `dark`, `light`, `one-atom-dark-conservative`, `one-atom-dark-full`, `one-dark-two-conservative`, `one-dark-two-full`. The function is a static import, not gated behind session lifecycle, so it's callable from the provider at any time.

### Revised smallest high-value scope

**One deliverable, two concerns:**

1. **`"tool"` completion domain** for `--tools` and `--exclude-tools`, backed by `() => pi.getAllTools()`. These have zero completion today (no domain, silent fallthrough). The catalog is live, named, session-accurate, and already accessible through the same `pi` reference that `registerAgentAutocomplete` captures.

2. **Comma-separated multi-value UX** as part of the tool domain, since it's how the CLI consumes these values.

These two are joined at the hip: you can't ship tool completion without comma support, and comma support has no other consumer yet. Implementing them together is one coherent vertical slice.

**Why skill/prompt-template/theme named pickers are second-scope, not first:**

They already have functioning filesystem completion. The upgrade from path browsing to a named catalog is a quality-of-life improvement, not a gap fix. The UX also has a design question the tool domain doesn't: when the user starts typing a path-like fragment (`/`, `~`, `.`), the named catalog becomes irrelevant and filesystem completion should take over. That dual-mode fallback is a new interaction pattern worth getting right separately, not bolted onto the first comma-list deliverable.

### Comma-list acceptance UX

The non-surprising behavior, consistent with how comma-separated values work in other CLIs and editors:

**After accepting a tool from the menu, insert `name,` (trailing comma, no space) and immediately reopen the menu with already-listed tools excluded.** The user continues picking, and ends the list by pressing Space.

Step by step:

```
/agent --tools |          → menu shows all tools
accept "read"  →  /agent --tools read,|          → menu reopens (read excluded)
accept "write" →  /agent --tools read,write,|     → menu reopens (read, write excluded)
press Space    →  /agent --tools read,write, |    → value ends, parser moves to next position
```

Why this works:
- The grammar's value token boundary is whitespace. A comma is just a character within the value. No grammar change needed.
- The CLI handles the trailing comma: `.split(",").map(s => s.trim()).filter(name => name.length > 0)` turns `"read,write,"` into `["read", "write"]`.
- The completion adapter owns the internal structure: fragment = text after last `,`, already-selected = parts before last `,`, replacement range = post-comma cursor span.
- Pressing Space is the universal "I'm done with this value" gesture — it matches how every other option value ends.

**Why not space-to-continue or a "Done" sentinel:**

Space-to-continue (accept `read`, then type `,` to keep going) requires the user to know the protocol and loses the eager-reopen benefit. A "Done" menu item is unfamiliar and wastes a slot. The comma-trail pattern is how tools like `fzf-tmux` and VS Code multi-select work — accept keeps the cursor in the value; escape/space ends it.

**Edge cases:**

- User types `--tools "read,wr|"` (quoted value): adapter splits on `,` inside the quotes identically.
- User types `--tools read` then Space (no comma): single-tool allowlist, value is `"read"`, parser advances normally.
- Empty catalog (no tools loaded): empty menu, falls through to native provider.

1	# `/agent` command-line parser — specification
2	
3	This is the authoritative spec for how the shared command-line engine interprets
4	submitted `/agent` / `/agent-isolated` input and pre-submit editor input. Runtime parsing
5	and eager autocomplete both derive option names, arity, aliases, roles, and value domains
6	from the declaration in `command-line.ts`.
7	
8	## 1. What the parser produces
9	
10	```ts
11	type ParsedAgentCommand = {
12	  isolate: boolean;          // -i / --isolate
13	  context: boolean;          // -c / --context
14	  forwardedArgs: string[];   // recognized pi option tokens (+values) in input order, e.g. ["--thinking","high"]
15	  task: string;              // the prose prompt (backslash escapes applied, quotes kept). Never empty.
16	  warnings: string[];        // advisory messages (see §5). May be empty.
17	};
18	```
19	
20	`forwardedArgs` contains **only** known, non-blocked pi options — never the extension's own
21	options, never unknown/third-party tokens. It is later mapped to child-session inputs by
22	`resolveForwardedOptions` (unchanged in spirit, but the unknown-flag path is removed).
23	
24	## 2. The state machine (one-way: args → prose)
25	
26	Read whitespace-delimited tokens from the front. Start in **args mode**.
27	
28	- In args mode, classify each token (§4). A recognized option is consumed (with its value if it
29	  takes one) and we stay in args mode.
30	- The **first** token that is not a recognized option flips us to **prose mode**, permanently.
31	  There is no path back to args mode.
32	- **Prose** is the remainder of the original input starting at the flip token, kept verbatim
33	  except for backslash-escape processing (§6). Whitespace and quotes are preserved exactly.
34	
35	If options are consumed and nothing is left, that is a usage error (a task is required).
36	When the very first token is prose, the entire original input is the task, including any
37	leading whitespace (unchanged from today).
38	
39	## 3. Recognized options
40	
41	### 3a. Extension-owned and normalized options
42	| Token(s) | Arity | Effect |
43	|---|---|---|
44	| `-m`, `--model` | value | Added to `forwardedArgs` as canonical `--model <value>` |
45	| `-i`, `--isolate` | boolean | Consumed here; `isolate = true` |
46	| `-c`, `--context` | boolean | Consumed here; `context = true` |
47	
48	`-m` and `--model` are one semantic option. Both resolve once through Pi's
49	`resolveCliModel()` path, and a preceding `--provider` scopes either spelling. `-c` is the
50	extension's; pi's own `-c` (continue) is intentionally shadowed and unavailable. A model
51	option with no value and no remaining task ends in the normal **usage error**.
52	
53	### 3b. Known pi options — declared statically; added to `forwardedArgs`
54	**Value-taking** (consume the next token as the value):
55	`--provider`, `--api-key`, `--system-prompt`, `--append-system-prompt`, `--mode`,
56	`--name`/`-n`, `--session`, `--session-id`, `--fork`, `--session-dir`, `--tools`/`-t`,
57	`--exclude-tools`/`-xt`, `--thinking`, `--extension`/`-e`, `--skill`, `--prompt-template`.
58	
59	**Boolean** (consume no value):
60	`--continue`, `--resume`/`-r`, `--no-session`, `--no-tools`/`-nt`, `--no-builtin-tools`/`-nbt`,
61	`--no-extensions`/`-ne`, `--no-skills`/`-ns`, `--no-prompt-templates`/`-np`, `--no-themes`,
62	`--no-context-files`/`-nc`, `--verbose`, `--approve`/`-a`, `--no-approve`/`-na`, `--offline`,
63	`--print`/`-p`.
64	
65	Notes:
66	- The shared declaration is a snapshot of `pi --help`; it is maintained by hand. There is no
67	  runtime dependency on pi's parser for recognition or arity.
68	- **Reading a value** (applies to every value-taking option, including both model spellings):
69	  the value is the token immediately after the option. If that token **begins with a quote char**
70	  (§6a) and a matching close quote appears later, the value is the text between the quotes —
71	  spanning internal whitespace — with the surrounding quotes **removed**; its content is literal
72	  (no arg parsing, no backslash processing inside — WYSIWYG). Otherwise the value is the next
73	  whitespace-delimited token, verbatim (consumed even if it looks like another option, e.g.
74	  `--thinking --offline` sets thinking's value to `--offline`). There is **no** distinction between
75	  "single-value" and "multi-value" options — every value-taking option reads its value this way, so
76	  `-m gpt56s` ≡ `-m "gpt56s"` and `--system-prompt Psych` ≡ `--system-prompt "Psych"`.
77	  The dequoted value is stored as **one element** in `forwardedArgs`
78	  (e.g. `["--system-prompt", "I am psyched"]`), so pi's `parseArgs` maps it as a single value.
79	  If a value opens with a quote but has no matching close, fall back to the whitespace-delimited token.
80	- `--print`/`-p` is modeled as **boolean** here (pi's optional-value form would eat prose).
81	
82	Value examples:
83	- `--system-prompt "I am psyched"` → value `I am psyched`.
84	- `--system-prompt "talk about -m modelname arg"` → value `talk about -m modelname arg` (inner `-m` not parsed).
85	- `--system-prompt "talk about \-m arg"` → value `talk about \-m arg` (backslash kept; no recursion).
86	- `-m "gpt56s"` → `forwardedArgs` contains `--model`, `gpt56s`.
87	
88	### 3c. Blocked pi options — rejected
89	`--theme <path>`, `--models`, `--export`, `--list-models`, `-h`/`--help`, `-v`/`--version`.
90	Appearing in **args mode** (leading) → hard **error** for either command:
91	`"/<command> does not support <opt>; it would disrupt the background agent run."`
92	
93	Blocked options stay declared so prose advisories remain truthful. In particular, singular
94	`--theme` is declared value-taking: `do it --theme ./theme.json` warns about
95	`--theme ./theme.json`, not just the option name. `--no-themes` is a separate supported
96	boolean and remains forwarded.
97	
98	## 4. Classifying a leading token (args mode), in order
99	1. **Escaped** (starts with a quote char, or is a backslash-before-dash word) → prose; **flip**. No warning. (§6)
100	2. **Extension-owned or normalized option** (§3a) → consume (+ model value); stay in args mode.
101	3. **Blocked pi option** (§3c) → **error**.
102	4. **Known pi option** (§3b) → consume (+ value if value-taking); push raw token(s) to `forwardedArgs`; stay in args mode.
103	5. **Anything else** — unknown `--foo` / `-x`, or a non-dash word → **flip to prose**; no warning.
104	
105	## 5. Warnings (prose mode only) — exactly one kind
106	While in prose mode, if an **unescaped, unquoted** token is a **recognized** option
107	(extension §3a, known §3b, or blocked §3c), append this advisory:
108	
109	> ``<opt> [<value>] was included in the prompt body. To specify an argument or an option, place it at the beginning of the command input: /<command> <opt> [<value>] <first-prose-word> …``
110	
111	- `<value>` appears only for value-taking options; it is the token that immediately follows in the input.
112	- `<first-prose-word>` is the first whitespace-delimited word of the prose.
113	- `<command>` is the actual command (`agent` or `agent-isolated`).
114	- Unknown arg-looking tokens in prose (`-g`, `--doesnotexist`) → **no** warning.
115	- Quoted or backslash-escaped option-looking tokens → **no** warning.
116	- Warnings never change the prose text.
117	
118	Worked examples:
119	- `hello world -m gpt56s` → task = whole string; warn `-m gpt56s`, suggest `/agent -m gpt56s hello …`.
120	- `-m gpt56s hello --thinking high world` → `-m gpt56s` parsed; task = `hello --thinking high world`;
121	  warn `--thinking high`, suggest `/agent --thinking high hello …`.
122	- `-g badflagname hello world` → `-g` unknown → task = whole string; **no** warning.
123	- `hello world -g badflagname` → task = whole string; **no** warning.
124	- `--doesnotexist this is my message` → `--doesnotexist` unknown → task = whole string; **no** warning.
125	
126	## 6. Escaping — opt a token out of arg parsing. NEVER recurses.
127	
128	### 6a. Quotes — kept in prose; stripped ONLY when reading an option value
129	Quote chars: `` ` `` `'` `"` `‘` `’` `“` `”`. Matched pairs: `"…"`, `'…'`, `` `…` ``, `‘…’`, `“…”`.
130	- Inside a matched quote span: no token is treated as an option, and no warning fires.
131	- In **prose**, quotes are **kept verbatim** — they are ordinary characters that merely suppress
132	  arg parsing. The one exception is when a quote span is being read as an **option's value**
133	  (§3b): there the surrounding quotes are removed and the content becomes the value.
134	- Content inside quotes is literal; a backslash inside quotes is **not** processed (kept).
135	- A quoted span at the very start (not an option value) still flips to prose.
136	- An unmatched quote is just a literal character (no span, no effect).
137	
138	Examples:
139	- `summarize "war and peace"` → task `summarize "war and peace"` (prose → quotes kept).
140	- `"\-m gpt56 hello"` (leading, not a value) → task `"\-m gpt56 hello"` (quotes kept, backslash kept, no arg parsing inside).
141	- `--system-prompt "war and peace"` → value `war and peace` (value → quotes stripped).
142	
143	### 6b. Backslash-before-dash — the backslash IS removed
144	A backslash at the start of a word whose next char is `-` escapes that word:
145	- Remove the leading `\`; the word (now starting with `-`) is prose. Flip to prose if in args mode;
146	  if already in prose, still remove the backslash and emit no warning.
147	- Overly-cautious double form: after removing the leading `\` before `-`, if the next two chars are
148	  `\-`, remove that `\` too. So `\-\-word` → `--word`. One backslash also suffices: `\--word` → `--word`.
149	- A backslash **inside quotes** is not processed (see §6a).
150	- A backslash NOT immediately before a `-` is left literal (not an escape).
151	
152	Examples:
153	- `\-m` → `-m`;  `\--thinking` → `--thinking`;  `\-\-thinking` → `--thinking`.
154	- `hello agent, \-m "gpt56s" how are you?` → `hello agent, -m "gpt56s" how are you?`.
155	- `hello agent, \--thi"nking" high` → `hello agent, --thi"nking" high`.
156	
157	## 7. Application layer (`resolveForwardedOptions`) — simplified
158	`forwardedArgs` (known pi options only) is mapped to child-session inputs. The application
159	layer maps thinking, model/provider through `resolveCliModel`, tools/excludeTools/noTools,
160	and `resourceLoaderOptions` (system prompt, skills, extensions, prompt templates, and
161	supported no-* toggles including `--no-themes`). Singular `--theme` never reaches this
162	projection. There is no unknown-flag / `extensionFlagValues` path or runtime arity probe;
163	recognition and arity come from the shared declaration.
164	
165	## 8. Wiring
166	- `parseAgentCommand` is pure and returns `warnings`.
167	- `startUserAgent` emits each warning via `ctx.ui.notify(warning, "warning")` inside the existing
168	  `if (ctx.hasUI)` block. Parse/blocked/usage errors keep flowing through `handleAgentCommand`'s
169	  try/catch to `reportCommandError` (unchanged).
170	
171	## 9. Edge decisions (locked)
172	- Bare `-m` (no value) → usage error.
173	- Empty task after consuming options → usage error.
174	- Blocked option leading → hard error; in prose → warning.
175	- No `--` options terminator (backslash/quotes handle "task starts with a dash").
176	- Value-taking option with no following token → the option is still recorded (no value); no crash.
177	- Multiple known options in prose → one warning per occurrence, in order.
178	
179	## 10. Pre-submit cursor analysis and eager autocomplete
180	
181	Cursor analysis recognizes only exact `/agent` and `/agent-isolated` command lines. It
182	preserves the active token's source span and reports either an option fragment, a value
183	fragment with its owning declaration, or no completion once parsing has entered terminal
184	prose. Quoted and backslash-escaped dashes therefore never reopen option completion.
185	
186	Typing `-` at a valid option position explicitly opens the menu without Tab. A single `-`
187	may match short and long spellings; `--` matches long spellings only. Every alias is shown as
